abstract: <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of digital systems, cloud platforms, and interconnected networks has significantly increased the complexity and impact of cybersecurity threats. Traditional security mechanisms, largely signature- or rule-based, are often insufficient to detect novel or evolving attacks and suffer from high false-positive rates. To address these limitations, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques have emerged as powerful tools for proactive, adaptive, and scalable cybersecurity defense. This paper investigates the application of various ML algorithms, including classical models (SVM, Decision Trees, Random Forest), ensemble methods (Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost), and deep learning architectures (Multi-Layer Perceptrons, Convolutional Neural Networks), for threat detection using publicly available datasets such as NSL-KDD and CICIDS2017. The methodology encompasses data preprocessing, feature selection, model training, and evaluation using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Experimental results demonstrate that ensemble and deep learning models outperform traditional classifiers in detecting complex cyber threats while minimizing false positives. The study highlights the effectiveness of AI/ML-driven cybersecurity systems and discusses potential future directions, including real-time threat detection, IoT/cloud integration, hybrid architectures, and explainable AI. These findings provide insights into designing robust, adaptive, and interpretable security solutions capable of addressing evolving cyber threats.</jats:p>
title: AI & MACHINE LEARNING IN CYBERSECURITY
